sentences.text:
Learned counsel for the applicants submits that applicant no. 5 is wife of opposite party no. 2 /
complainant and essentially the matter pertains to the matrimonial dispute.

The applicant no. 5 has lodged a first information report under Sections 323, 325, 504 I.P.C. against the opposite party no. 2 and his family members on 28.09.2013 and one case was lodged under Section- 498A, 406, 323,
504, 506 I.P.C. and after investigation the charge sheet had been submitted against the accused persons.

The applicant no. 5 has also filed a case under Section 125 Cr.P.C. against opposite party no. 2 in the year 2012 and one case was filed under Domestic Violence Act, whereas opposite party no. 2 has filed a case under Section 13 of Hindu Marriage Act.
It was submitted that the impugned complaint has been lodged as a counterblast to the cases lodged by the applicant no. 5.
Only general allegations have been levelled against all accused persons and entire family of applicant no. 5 has been roped in.

It was submitted that the impugned proceedings have been instituted with mala fide intention in order to exert undue pressure on the applicant no. 5 and thus, the impugned proceedings are liable to be quashed.
4. Learned counsel for opposite party no. 2/ complainant has opposed the application and submitted that in the alleged incident, the complainant has sustained injuries and he was medically examined.

There is evidence that on 08.02.2007 the applicants came at the house of the sister of the complainant and they have assaulted the complainant and his golden chain, ring and cash of Rs.
2,000/- were snatched by the accused persons.
The version of the complainant is supported by medical evidence.

It was further submitted that the impugned summoning order has been passed by considering the material on record and there is no illegality or perversity in the same.
5.
I have considered the rival submissions and perused the record.

6. Section - 482 Cr.PC. saves the inherent power of the High Court to make such orders as may be necessary to give effect to any order under this Code, or to prevent abuse of the process of any court or otherwise to secure the ends of justice.

Hon'ble Apex Court in State of Karnataka v. L.
Muniswamy (1977) 2 SCC 699

entities.text:
State of Karnataka v. L.
Muniswamy (1977) 2 SCC 699
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: held that the High Court is entitled to quash a proceeding if it comes to the conclusion that allowing the proceeding to continue would be an abuse of the process of the Court or that the ends of justice require that the proceeding ought to be quashed.

In para 7 of the judgment, the Court held :-
''7. ...

In the exercise of this wholesome power, the High Court is entitled to quash a proceeding if it comes to the conclusion that allowing the proceeding to continue would be an abuse of the process of the court or that the ends of justice require that the proceeding ought to be quashed.

The saving of the High Court's inherent powers,
both in civil and criminal matters, is designed to achieve a salutary public purpose which is that a court proceeding ought not to be permitted to degenerate into a weapon of harassment or persecution.''

In landmark judgment of State of Haryana v. Bhajan Lal 1992 Supp (1) SCC 335, the Court held as under:
"102.

entities.text: State of Haryana v. Bhajan Lal 1992 Supp (1) SCC 335
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the backdrop of the interpretation of the various relevant provisions of the Code under Chapter XIV and of the principles of law enunciated by this Court in a series of decisions relating to the exercise of the extraordinary power under Article 226 or the inherent powers under Section 482 of the Code which we have extracted and reproduced above, we give the following categories of cases by way of illustration wherein such power could be exercised either to prevent abuse of the process of any court or otherwise to secure the ends of justice, though it may not be possible to lay down any precise, clearly defined and sufficiently channelised and inflexible guidelines or rigid formulae and to give an exhaustive list of myriad kinds of cases wherein such power should be exercised.

(1) Where the allegations made in the first information report or the complaint, even if they are taken at their face value and accepted in their entirety do not prima facie constitute any offence or make out a case against the accused.

(2) Where the allegations in the first information report and other materials, if any,
accompanying the FIR do not disclose a cognizable offence, justifying an investigation by police officers under Section 156(1) of the Code except under an order of a Magistrate within the purview of Section 155(2) of the Code.

(3) Where the uncontroverted allegations made in the FIR or complaint and the evidence collected in support of the same do not disclose the commission of any offence and make out a case against the accused.

(4) Where, the allegations in the FIR do not constitute a cognizable offence but constitute only a non-cognizable offence, no investigation is permitted by a police officer without an order of a Magistrate as contemplated under Section 155(2) of the Code.

(5) Where the allegations made in the FIR or complaint are so absurd and inherently improbable on the basis of which no prudent person can ever reach a just conclusion that there is sufficient ground for proceeding against the accused.

(6) Where there is an express legal bar engrafted in any of the provisions of the Code or the concerned Act (under which a criminal proceeding is instituted) to the institution and continuance of the proceedings and/or where there is a specific provision in the Code or the concerned Act, providing efficacious redress for the grievance of the aggrieved party.

(7) Where a criminal proceeding is manifestly attended with mala fide and/or where the proceeding is maliciously instituted with an ulterior motive for wreaking Rajiv @ Raju Yadav And 7 Ors. vs State Of U.P. And Anr. on 11 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/123924913/

8. The principles culled out by the Hon'ble Apex Court in above referred case have consistently been followed in the several judgments.

sentences.text: In State of Andhra Pradesh v. Golconda Linga Swamy, (2004) 6 SCC 522, it was observed that authority of the court exists for advancement of justice and if any attempt is made to abuse that authority so as to produce injustice, the court has power to prevent such abuse.

entities.text: State of Andhra Pradesh v. Golconda Linga Swamy, (2004) 6 SCC 522
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It would be an abuse of the process of the court to allow any action which would result in injustice and prevent promotion of justice.
10. Keeping aforesaid legal position in view, in the instant matter on perusal of record, it appears that essentially the matter pertains to matrimonial dispute between the parties.
The applicant no.5 is wife of the opposite party no.2/complainant.

Applicant no.1 to 3 are brother of applicant no.5,
applicant no.4 and 8 are father and mother of applicant no.5 and applicant no.6 and 7 are sister-in-law (bhabhi) of applicant no.5.
It appears that the marriage of applicant no.5 with opposite party no.2/complainant has taken place on 29.05.2010 but there was some dispute between them.

Earlier, the applicant no.5 has lodged a case against the opposite party no.2/complainant and his family members vide Crime No. 596 of 2013, under Sections ? 323, 325, 504 I.P.C. and in that matter charge sheet was submitted.

Another first information report was lodged by applicant no.5 vide Crime No. 85 of 2013, under Sections ? 498-A, 406, 323, 504, 506 I.P.C. and 3/4 D. P. Act against the opposite party no.2/complainant and his family members and in that matter also charge sheet was submitted.

One case was lodged by the applicant no.5 under Section ? 125 Cr.P.C. and one more case was lodged by the applicant no.5 under Section ? 12 of Domestic Violence Act against the opposite party no.2 /complainant.
It appears that the opposite party no.2 has also filed a case under Section ? 13 of The Hindu Marriage Act.

The opposite party no.2/complainant has lodged complaint of the impugned case on 06.03.2017, making allegations that on 08.02.2017 all the applicants came at the house of his sister and they have assaulted the complainant and forcibly took away the complainant to their home and they have assaulted him.
It was also alleged that the applicants have snatched chain, ring and Rs.2,000/- from complainant.
It was further alleged in the complaint that they have threatened him to execute a sale deed of his property and they have obtained his signature on some blank papers.

Only a vague allegation has been made that all the applicants, which include Rajiv @ Raju Yadav And 7 Ors. vs State Of U.P. And Anr. on 11 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/123924913/

sentences.text: 4 applicant no.5 and her father, mother, brothers and sisters-in-law, have assaulted the complainant and snatched the aforesaid articles and amount of Rs. 2,000/-.
No specific role has been assigned to any of the accused.
Prima facie the allegations made by the complainant are absurd and inherently improbable.
It cannot be believed that a lady and her father, mother, brothers and sisters-in-law would commit such an incident against husband of that lady.

It is apparent that several cases have already been lodged by the applicant No. 5 against the opposite party No. 2 / complainant and after that the opposite party No. 2 has lodged the impugned complaint.

The attending facts clearly show that the opposite party no.2/complainant has lodged the impugned complaint as a counter blast in order to settle score and the impugned proceedings are manifestly attended with malafide and the same were maliciously instituted with an ulterior motive, wrecking vengeance on the applicants-accused.
The instant matter is squarely covered in aforesaid category (7) of the judgment of case of Bhajan Lal (supra).

As stated earlier, in exercise of the powers the Court would be justified to quash any proceeding if it finds that initiation or continuance of it amounts to abuse of the process of court or quashing of these proceedings would otherwise serve the ends of justice.
In the present matter, considering entire facts of matter a case for quashing of impugned proceedings is made out.
11. In view of aforesaid, the entire impugned proceedings including summoning order of aforesaid complaint case are hereby quashed.
12. The application under Section ? 482 Cr.P.C. is allowed.
